marketingRemarks.marketingRemark: Prime industrial lot located in Merced's growing southeast corridor! This 1.32-acre (57,543 sq ft) parcel is zoned M-2 Heavy Industrial, ideal for warehouse, manufacturing, trucking, or distribution uses. The site offers level topography, street frontage, and excellent access to major transportation routes including Highway 99, Highway 140, and Highway 59, with the new Campus Parkway providing direct connection to UC Merced and surrounding development areas.  Located within the City of Merced's Sphere of Influence, this parcel lies in a rapidly developing area with strong growth potential for industrial and commercial projects. Utilities are nearby (buyer to verify connection points). The property's zoning allows a wide range of industrial uses, making it a versatile opportunity for investors, builders, or owner-users.

marketingRemarks.marketingRemark: Location is key! This 1.32-acre lot is poised for significant growth in Southeast Merced, situated within the path of development and within the City of Merced's Sphere of Influence/General Plan. It lies near the new 37-acre sports complex and the Gateway Marketplace regional shopping center. Major arterial routes like Hwy 99, Hwy 59, Hwy 140, and the UC Merced Campus Parkway are conveniently close. Merced's industrial market is underserved, leading to a high demand for industrial properties. The zoning for this vacant lot is M-2, heavy industrial, and it is encircled by established industrial properties.

schoolReviews.review: I have 2 students here. The one senior and one freshman. I like that it is the type of school where most students know each other from their younger days and yet, they have been welcoming to students like mine, who are transplants. Parents seem to be engaged, FFA seems great and there are lots of programs, clubs and pathways for students to explore.

This is an amazing campus to work at. I feel supported by both administration and parents, which is not always the case at other schools. I have some of the best kids in the district in my classes and for the most part, they all work hard and do their best. This is a wonderful school!!!

My son is in his 3rd year at Charles Wright and my daughter in her 2nd year, and we have had nothing but excellent experiences with all of the teachers, and with the principal, Mrs. Slaven, and Assistant Principal, Mrs. Barber. There is also a very active Parent Teacher Club that has raised several thousand dollars over the past 3 years, money that has been used to improve the playground equipment, provide teachers with supplies and classroom tools, and most importantly, restored the ability of all classes to go on big field trips several times throughout the year! My kids and I love Charles Wright! Staying involved and getting to know the teachers, principals, and staff is key, and has allowed us to benefit from constant support and opportunities to improve. Only a handful of parents come to the PTC meetings, and attendance of school functions by families of students seems low.

schoolGranularRatings.schoolGranularRatingCopyText: Students at this school are making less academic progress from one grade to the next compared to similar students in the state.
schoolGranularRatings.schoolGranularRatingsDescription: The Student Progress Rating measures whether students at this school are making academic progress over time based on student growth data provided by the Department of Education. Specifically, this rating looks at how much progress individual students have made on state assessments during the past year or more, how this performance aligns with expected progress based on a student growth model established by the state Department of Education, and how this school's growth data compares to other schools in the state. The Growth Rating was created using 2025 Student growth data from California Department of Education.

schoolGranularRatings.schoolGranularRatingCopyText: Underserved students at this school may be falling behind other students in the state, and this school may have achievement gaps between different student groups.
schoolGranularRatings.schoolGranularRatingsDescription: Using the state’s Department of Education data, the Equity Overview Rating compares this school to other schools in the state by looking at how well this school serves the needs of disadvantaged students relative to all students using state proficiency tests, student growth or academic progress data, and college readiness data. The Equity Rating was created using 2025 California Assessment of Student Performance and Progress (CAASPP) data from California Department of Education, using 2025 4-year high school graduation rate data from California Department of Education, using 2025 Student growth data from California Department of Education, using 2025 Percent of students who meet UC/CSU entrance requirements data from California Department of Education, using 2025 California Science Test data from California Department of Education, using 2023 demographic data from the National Center for Education Statistics, and using 2025 demographic data from California Department of Education.

buyingPowerInfo.affordabilityDisclaimer:
We use your income and monthly debt to come up with your debt-to-income ratio, or DTI. We base your buying power on your DTI. We calculate your buying power based on a DTI of 36%, which is the general rule around how much of your income should go toward debt.

The ranges below will help you understand if you have enough income to live comfortably for the selected home price. A general guide is to budget around 28% of your pre-tax income for your mortgage payment, and another 8% for other debts.

Affordable: 0%-36%
Stretch: 37%-50%
Ambitious: Above 50%
